A feature release that syncs the SDK with Python SDK v0.2.168 (from v0.2.160).
It adds typed outputs for 14 more hook events, new fields on the hook inputs,
and a typed view of the session `init` message. It also fixes
`SandboxSettings.ignoreViolations`, which never matched the CLI's schema.

## ⚠️ Behavior and compatibility changes

**`SandboxIgnoreViolations` is now a command-pattern map**
([Python #1380](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1380)).
The old `{file, network}` shape was sent to the CLI as
`{"file": [...], "network": [...]}`. The CLI reads those keys as *command
patterns*, so it only suppressed violations for commands whose text contained
the words "file" or "network". The CLI's actual schema maps a command pattern
(`"*"` for every command) to substrings of the violation text. Both checks are
plain substring matches, and the setting changes which violations are
reported, not what the sandbox blocks.

```java
// Leave violations mentioning /etc/hosts unreported for every command
SandboxIgnoreViolations.forAllCommands(List.of("/etc/hosts"))

// Or per command pattern
SandboxIgnoreViolations.of(Map.of(
    "*", List.of("/etc/hosts"),
    "npm test", List.of("registry.npmjs.org")))
```

- The record now has a single `patterns` component and serializes as the bare
  map.
- The `file()` and `network()` accessors are gone.
- The two-list constructor still compiles. It is deprecated for removal and
  now does what its parameters described: it puts both lists under `"*"`.
  Code that relied on the old (broken) behavior will see more violations
  suppressed, never fewer blocked.

**Hook input records gained components.** Every hook input record has new
components at the end (see below). Each keeps its previous canonical signature
as a constructor overload, so source that calls those constructors compiles
unchanged. The same applies to `UserPromptSubmitHookSpecificOutput`, which
keeps its one-argument constructor. Code that deconstructs these records with
record patterns, or that was compiled against the old canonical constructors,
needs a recompile.

## Highlights

**Typed outputs for 14 more hook events**
([Python #1331](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1331)).
`HookSpecificOutput` now has 21 permitted records. The new ones:

| Event | Fields |
|-------|--------|
| `SessionStart` | `additionalContext`, `initialUserMessage`, `sessionTitle`, `watchPaths`, `reloadSkills` |
| `UserPromptExpansion` | `additionalContext`, `suppressOriginalPrompt` |
| `PostToolBatch`, `PostModelSwitch` | `additionalContext` |
| `Stop`, `SubagentStop` | `additionalContext`: non-error feedback that keeps the model going |
| `PermissionDenied` | `retry` |
| `PreModelSwitch` | `permissionDecision` (allow, deny or ask; `DEFER` is rejected), `permissionDecisionReason` |
| `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult` | `action` (new `ElicitationAction` enum), `content` |
| `CwdChanged`, `FileChanged` | `watchPaths` |
| `WorktreeCreate` | `worktreePath` (required) |
| `MessageDisplay` | `displayContent` |

`UserPromptSubmitHookSpecificOutput` also gains `sessionTitle` and
`suppressOriginalPrompt`.

```java
HookOutput.builder()
    .hookSpecificOutput(new StopHookSpecificOutput("Tests still fail; keep going."))
    .build();
```

> As in the Python SDK, `HookEvent` is unchanged: SDK hook callbacks still
> register for its ten events. Most of the new types describe outputs for
> events a Java callback cannot receive yet. They are typed now for parity
> with the Python and TypeScript SDKs.

**New hook input fields**
([Python #1331](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1331)).
Each is `null` when the CLI omits it.

- Every `HookInput` reports `promptId()`, the prompt's UUID (it matches
  `prompt.id` on OpenTelemetry events), and `effort()`, a new `HookEffort`
  record holding the turn's effort `level`.
- `PostToolUseHookInput` and `PostToolUseFailureHookInput` gain `durationMs`:
  the tool's execution time, excluding permission prompts and hooks.
- `StopHookInput` and `SubagentStopHookInput` gain `lastAssistantMessage`,
  `backgroundTasks` (`BackgroundTaskSummary`) and `sessionCrons`
  (`SessionCronSummary`). A Stop hook can now see what work is still in flight
  and which scheduled wakeups will resume the session.

**`SystemInitData`**
([Python #1332](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-agent-sdk-python/pull/1332)).
A typed view of the `system`/`init` message, which carries the model, cwd,
tools, MCP servers, plugins and plugin load failures, slash commands,
permission mode, fast mode state and the CLI's `capabilities` list:

```java
if (msg instanceof SystemMessage system) {
    SystemInitData init = system.initData();   // null unless subtype is "init"
    if (init != null && init.capabilities() != null
            && init.capabilities().contains("interrupt_receipt_v1")) {
        // feature-detect instead of comparing claudeCodeVersion()
    }
}
```

The parser still returns a plain `SystemMessage`, and the payload is not
validated. A field the CLI omits is `null`, and an enum value this SDK does not
recognize reads as `null`. The raw value always stays in `data()`.

## Also in this release

- **`includeHookEvents` Javadoc** now notes that the CLI emits the
  `SessionStart` and `Setup` hook events regardless of the setting.
- **`IncludePartialMessagesExample`** requests summarized thinking with
  `ThinkingConfigEnabled(8000, ThinkingDisplay.SUMMARIZED)`. Since Claude Code
  2.1.287, thinking text is omitted unless requested: the `thinking_delta`
  events still arrive, but empty.
- **`VerbatimPromptsExample`** checks the session transcript, not just the
  model's reply. The CLI records an expanded `@`-mention as a `file`
  attachment, and the model sometimes answers UNKNOWN even when the file was
  attached.
- **README fixes**, in English and all five translations. The hook example
  called a `HookSpecificOutput.preToolUse()` builder that does not exist, and
  the sandbox example did not compile. Both now compile, and the
  message-handling example shows `SystemMessage.initData()`.
- **Tests:** 1140. New tests check every hook output's and init payload's
  JSON key sets against the Python SDK's required and optional keys, and check
  that `ignoreViolations` reaches `--settings` as the bare map. All examples
  were run against Claude Code 2.1.303.
